VERDICT: REFUTED  
NEIGHBOR: [4]  
EVIDENCE: "Rather than simply shorten a sentence by deleting words or constituents, as in previous work, we rewrite it using additional operations such as substitution, reordering, and insertion." This neighbor investigates sentence rewriting techniques, which aligns with the purpose of preserving information through caption condensation, suggesting that rewriting can succeed where filtering fails.

VERDICT: REFUTED  
NEIGHBOR: [4]  
EVIDENCE: "What Makes 'Good' Distractors for Object Hallucination Evaluation in Large Vision-Language Models? ... The most commonly used Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation (POPE) benchmark evaluates this issue by sampling negative categories according to category-level statistics." This neighbor investigates object hallucination in vision-language models using the POPE benchmark, which is directly related to the contribution's focus on object-presence mentions and the POPE recall metric.

VERDICT: REFUTED  
NEIGHBOR: 7  
EVIDENCE: "Kitty: Accurate and Efficient 2-bit KV Cache Quantization with Dynamic Channel-wise Precision Boost — The KV cache is a dominant memory bottleneck for LLM inference. While 4-bit KV quantization preserves accuracy, 2-bit often degrades it, especially on long-context reasoning. We close this gap via an algorithm-system co-design for mixed-precision KV caching: Kitty. On the algorithm side, extensive experiments show that Dynamic Channel-wise Precision Boost -- which ranks Key-cache channels by sensitivity and keeps only a small fraction at higher precision -- maintains near-zero loss in accuracy d" This neighbor investigates the same empirical relationship between static and dynamic methods in the context of KV cache quantization, focusing on accuracy outcomes, thus covering the purpose.

VERDICT: REFUTED  
NEIGHBOR: [12]  
EVIDENCE: "Vision Transformers have achieved state-of-the-art performance in many visual tasks... To overcome these limitations, we propose key-only attention, which excludes query-key pairwise interactions and uses a compute-efficient saliency-gate to obtain attention weights, modeling local-global interaction." This neighbor investigates query-key interactions in Vision Transformers, similar to the contribution's focus on addressing issues with query-key interactions in linear attention.

VERDICT: REFUTED  
NEIGHBOR: [10]  
EVIDENCE: "Herein, we introduce Visual Tokens Withdrawal (VTW), a plug-and-play module to boost MLLMs for rapid inference. Our approach is inspired by two intriguing phenomena we have observed: (1) the attention sink phenomenon that is prevalent in LLMs also persists in MLLMs, suggesting that initial tokens and their associated attention weights dominate the computation; (2) the computational cost of visual tokens can be significantly reduced without degrading performance." This work addresses the inefficiency of MLLM inference by compressing visual tokens, which aligns with the purpose of the contribution to improve MLLM efficiency by addressing token-related computational bottlenecks.

VERDICT: REFUTED  
NEIGHBOR: [7]  
EVIDENCE: "To address this, we propose an optimization-based objective for defending LLMs against jailbreaking attacks and an algorithm, Robust Prompt Optimization (RPO) to create robust systems." This neighbor shares the purpose of providing a tool for robust prompt evaluation against jailbreaking attacks, aligning with the contribution's objective of assessing prompt robustness across defenses and models.

VERDICT: REFUTED  
NEIGHBOR: [1]  
EVIDENCE: "To reduce this gap, we introduce activation engineering: the inference-time modification of activations in order to control (or steer) model outputs." This neighbor discusses activation engineering as a method to control model outputs, aligning with the contribution's purpose of unifying related literature under the 'activation engineering' methodology.

VERDICT: REFUTED  
NEIGHBOR: 13  
EVIDENCE: "Robotic Control via Embodied Chain-of-Thought Reasoning — A key limitation of learned robot control policies is their inability to generalize outside their training data. Recent works on vision-language-action models (VLAs) have shown that the use of large, internet pre-trained vision-language models as the backbone of learned robot policies can substantially improve their robustness and generalization ability." This neighbor pursues the same objective of enabling embodied agents to adapt their reasoning and planning in dynamic environments through chain-of-thought reasoning, aligning with the purpose of the contribution.
